Barking & Dagenham.method_notes: LBBD community infant/primary admission criteria (Starting school full-time 2026 booklet p23, Priority 3 and note 5; same in Admission Arrangements 2026-27 for Infant and Primary Schools): children who live closest to the school, measured in kilometres in a straight line (as the crow flies) using Synergy's GIS, from the centre of the child's home to the school's main gate; some addresses with different entry points use LLPG designated coordinates. Equal distances (e.g. flats) broken by lottery (random allocation). Priorities: EHCP named, looked-after, sibling (incl. linked infant/junior pairs), distance. Academies Eastbury Primary, Greatfields, James Cambell, Goresbrook, Sydney Russell, free school Riverside and George Carey CofE use the same criteria. Catholic schools (note 12) and St Margaret's CofE also measure straight line from centre of home to main gate for tie-breaks; Thames View Infants uses its own criteria. The statistics table states distances are in km, straight line.

Barnet.method_notes: Guide to Primary Education in Barnet 2027, 'Admission criteria for community primary schools in Barnet', Note 3: 'Distance is measured in a straight line between the address point for the child's home, supplied by Ordnance Survey, to the school's main gate (unless specified otherwise) using the Council's computerised geographical information system.' Community schools offer places first to children in the school's defined area (closest first), then to children outside it. The voluntary aided, free, foundation and academy schools set their own criteria (many faith-based, some with lotteries); their summaries in the guide also measure in a straight line. The council tables give the criterion under which the last place was offered: where that was a faith or lottery criterion, no places went on distance alone (no_distance_offers); where it was an open, community-band or 'any other applicant' criterion, the figure is recorded as a distance.

Bexley.method_notes: LB Bexley 'Before applying for a primary school place' (Admission to Primary Schools 2027-28), section 'Home-to-school distance': distance is measured in a straight line (as the crow flies) by the Council's GIS, from the NLPG easting/northing co-ordinates of the home address to the nearest school entrance approved by the Governors as an official entrance; measured in miles to three decimal places. Until 2015 most Bexley primaries used the shortest safe walking route; community, VC and most academies switched to straight line in 2015 and from 2016 all Bexley primary schools measure by straight line. Community/VC oversubscription criteria (Priority 5): nearest school entrance, straight line; equal distances for the last place decided by drawing lots; twins/multiple births treated as siblings. Home = address where the child lives with the main carer (Child Benefit). Academies, free schools and VA schools set their own criteria, but the council states the straight-line method applies to all primary schools.

Brent.method_notes: Brent Admission Arrangements for Community Schools 2026/27 ('Tie-break' Distance Measurement, p5): distance measured in a straight line from the address point in the property to the address point in the school, as determined by Local Land and Property Gazetteer (LLPG) data, using the measuring module of The Access Group admissions software (Ordnance Survey maps + LLPG, accurate to 1 cm); the arrangements also publish grid-reference measuring points (easting/northing) for each community school (p2). Nearer applicants have priority; where children are equidistant for the last place, computerised random allocation. The Sept 2027 primary handbook repeats straight-line measurement 'from a point in the property to a point in the school'. Exceptions in school entries in the handbook: Kilburn Grange (free school) uses the shortest walking route to the school's main entrance point; East Lane and Preston Manor measure from the front door of the home to school reception; NWL Jewish Day School to the main gate (straight line); Ark Franklin gives priority to Pupil Premium children within a 0.5-mile radius. Council tables give furthest distance per criterion in metres; furthest distance is not shown for looked-after, social/medical, pupil premium, staff children or 'nearest school with a vacancy' (directed) offers.

That is the furthest offer within that criterion, not necessarily the strict cut-off. The 2024 table lists criteria alphabetically within each school, not in priority order, so the general criterion (Any Other Applicant/Distance/Outside Catchment Area) was chosen; for Islamia, Princess Frederica and St Joseph's RC Infant the last faith/parish criterion was chosen by hand by matching the 2025-26 ordering. Bromley.method_notes: Bromley has no catchment areas and no community schools (all primaries are academies apart from two foundation schools, Edgebury and Poverest), so each school is its own admission authority. Primary Education in Bromley 2027-2028 booklet, 'Proximity, distance and all other children' (p.46): unless a school's arrangements say otherwise, distance is calculated in a straight line (as the crow flies) from the home address to the school using the Council's geographical information system (GIS), which uses the Council's gazetteer and Ordnance Survey address point data. The booklet does not specify the point at the school (gate/entrance/centroid) for the default; individual schools may define it (e.g. Southborough Primary: straight line to the main school gate). Some schools use random allocation within a criterion (booklet p.46). Coordinated scheme 2026/27 para 39: distance is from the child's permanent home address at the time of application. Distances in the booklet are in miles, as at the relevant national offer day.

City of London.method_notes: The City of London has only one state-funded primary, The Aldgate School (Sir John Cass's Foundation Primary until Sept 2020), a CofE VA school whose governing body sets its own arrangements; the City's School Admissions Team coordinates applications. Its oversubscription criteria (as printed in the City's 'Starting Primary School 2024/2025' booklets) are: 1 looked-after children; 2 siblings; 3-4 Church of England / other Christian worshippers by straight-line proximity; 5 City Child and Family Centre nursery children in the priority area; 6 children in the admissions priority area by shortest walking route; 7 staff children; 8 any other children by shortest walking route. The booklet notes also say the school uses the City of London GIS to measure straight-line distance from LLPG address point to the school's LLPG address point. The two statements conflict; the walking route is taken as the default because it governs criteria 6 and 8, where the last places went. The booklet figure is 'the furthest distance at which a Reception place was allocated' in metres.

Greenwich.gaps: 2025 figures not obtained: they would be in the 2026/27 booklet, which was not found online (the council now hosts the booklet only in a PageSuite reader showing the current 2027/28 edition, and the archived offers-map file from Aug 2025 still held 2024 data), so 2023 figures were added and every school's 2025 entry is not_published. Greenwich publishes a 'distance of last offer' for every school, including undersubscribed ones (e.g. Horn Park 2024: 65 applications for 60 places, 5723 m), and never 'all offered', so large values (e.g. Horn Park 13590.95 m, Cherry Orchard 12490.13 m in 2026) probably reflect the furthest offer made, not a real cut-off; recorded as printed. The 2027/28 booklet labels the 2026 figures 'for entry 2027'; they match the offers-map file labelled 2026. The archived 2024 map file disagreed with the booklet for Heronsgate (53781.35 vs 6907), Bishop John Robinson (21437.68 vs 2955) and Christ Church SE10 (1084.6 vs 4728), so booklet values were used; this suggests the 2026 map file (no independent source) could have similar errors. 2024 values are rounded to whole metres in the booklet. 2023 values come from a text PDF where some numbers ran into page numbers (e.g. Discovery '175816 17' read as 1758) - checked against page images for a sample only. 12 RC/CE faith schools have no published distance (not_published) and their own policies were not checked. Gallions Mount (on the 2026 map with no figure) and Holy Family RC are excluded as no longer open per GIAS. PAN = 'Reception places' in the 2025/26 booklet (Discovery and Montbelle PANs reduced from Sept 2026). Postcodes from the booklet/GIAS; split-site schools have one entry per site that admits Reception separately.

Hackney.method_notes: Hackney Education (home school distance page and Community Schools Admission Arrangements): home-to-school distance is measured in a straight line by a computerised distance-measuring system from the home address point (NLPG easting/northing, usually within the property footprint; one point per block of flats) to the main entrance of the school; the measuring point may not be the gate currently used. Community school oversubscription order: EHCP named, looked-after/previously looked-after, child protection plan, medical/social, siblings (community schools: if the family has moved since the sibling was offered, sibling priority only within 2 miles), children of staff, distance. Council says some schools and academies measure distance using other methods. Council tables give 'Max Distance (last child offered in miles)' only for community schools; VA schools and academies table gives applications/offers only.

Hackney.gaps: Council publishes cut-off distances only for the 32 community schools; the 18 VA schools and academies have no distance in any year, so they are 'not_published' unless the table shows non-preference offers or offers below places available (then 'all_offered'). Interpretation choices: a community school with non-preference offers, or with offers below places and no cap, is recorded as 'all_offered' (the printed max distance is kept in criterion_note) because vacancies remained after all applicants were placed; Hackney has falling rolls and many undersubscribed schools. Implausible printed distances on full schools (Hoxton Garden 2026: 350.333 miles; Parkwood 2024: 350.244 miles) recorded as not_published; other 350+/180 mile values (Millfields 2024/2025, Princess May 2025, Queensbridge 2025) fell on schools with non-preference offers and are recorded as all_offered. Capped schools (Hoxton Garden, Orchard, Princess May in 2026; Mandeville/Oldhill/Orchard/Princess May/Hoxton earlier) keep the distance even when offers < PAN. PAN = 'Total Places Available' in the 2026 table. Closed schools in earlier tables (Oldhill, Sir Thomas Abney, St Dominic's, St Mary's CofE - closed Aug 2025 per GIAS or absent from 2026 table) excluded. Postcodes and types from GIAS (Oct 2026). Per-school academy/VA measurement methods not researched (method 'unknown'). Distances are as printed in miles to 3 d.p.; criterion of the last offer is not given. The column is headed 'Max Distance (last child offered in miles)'; some full schools show large values (Gainsborough 2025 8.332, London Fields 2024 6.481, Queensbridge 2026 3.517, Shoreditch Park 2024 2.304) that may be the furthest child offered under a non-distance criterion (sibling/medical) rather than a true distance cut-off - recorded as printed, unverified.

Hammersmith & Fulham.method_notes: H&F Starting School 2026 brochure (common definitions / community schools policy, p.28-30) and community schools determined arrangements 2026/27: unless a school's own criteria say otherwise, distance is a straight line ('as the crow flies') from the child's home 'address point' (Ordnance Survey data) to the main entrance gate for pupils (community policy: nearest entrance for pupils), measured by H&F Council's computerised measuring system; nearest child gets highest priority. Shared address points (flats) are separated by random allocation/draw. The council's hints-and-tips leaflet states 'Distance is determined in straight line for all applications'. Community oversubscription order: looked after, exceptional need, siblings, children of staff, distance. Faith and free schools use foundation/open, nursery, Pupil Premium or multi-site categories (see school notes). Figures are in miles ('x of a mile').

Haringey.method_notes: Haringey Primary Admissions booklets (Sept 2026 and Sept 2027 entry), community school oversubscription criterion 5 'Distance' and Notes: distance measured in a straight line from the Ordnance Survey address point of the child's home to the Ordnance Survey address point of the school, calculated using the council's computerised mapping system; measurements by alternative systems or to other points are not taken into account. Tie-break within each criterion is home-school distance (same method); identical distances decided by random allocation supervised by an independent body. Community criteria order: LAC/previously LAC, exceptional social/medical, siblings, children of staff, distance. Some schools have a nursery criterion (e.g. Lift Trinity). Eden Primary (free school) and St James CofE (VA) use faith and distance bands; St Michael's CofE N6 uses a points-based faith criterion; Catholic/CofE VA and faith academies set their own criteria (not individually checked). The council's figure is the 'distance (in miles) from school of last child offered a place under distance criterion' on national offer day.

Harrow.method_notes: Harrow community school admission arrangements 2027/28, Part C (Definitions - Distance): distance measured in a straight line from home to school using a computerised mapping system based on Ordnance Survey data, from the unique address point of the home address to the centre point of the school site (council publishes maps of each school's centre point). Part A(ii) oversubscription criteria end with distance; tie-breaker within any criterion is straight-line distance, and equidistant applicants are separated by random computer selection. Primary Schools Guide 2025/26 states Harrow schools have no catchment areas and 'all schools in Harrow measure distances from home to school in a straight line from the home address to the school', usually to the centre point of the school (but it can be different in some cases). Council tables give furthest distance in miles where the distance criterion was applied as a tie-breaker; 'N/A' means distance was not needed. Faith VA schools, Catholic/CofE academies, Hujjat and St Jérôme (free schools) are reported only as 'contact the school'. Avanti House and Krishna Avanti (Hindu faith academies) are reported in full, with faith quotas before distance.

Havering.method_notes: Havering community infant and primary admission criteria 2027/28 (pp13-17, 'Distance of the home address from the school'): distance is measured in a straight line, not by walking or bus route, between a predetermined point for the school and the address point of the child's home; address points are at the centre of the home or the centre of a block of flats. Priorities: EHCP, looked-after/previously looked-after, exceptional medical/social, sibling (incl. partner infant/junior schools), staff children, then distance; distance also breaks ties within criteria 1-4; equal distances (same block of flats) decided by random draw by an officer not involved in admissions. The council's statistics tables label the furthest distance as 'Straight line distance' in km rounded to 3 decimal places, at initial allocation (16 April). Academies, free schools, the foundation school (Mawney) and faith schools set their own arrangements; not individually checked. The Drapers' academies have priority-area places (2024 table column).

Hillingdon.method_notes: LB Hillingdon Community Schools Determined Admission Arrangements 2026-27 ('Distance criterion', p.20): distance is measured in a straight line from the Ordnance Survey address point of the child's home to the agreed address point for the school, using the council's GIS (OS data). For blocks of flats with a communal entrance, the OS central point of the block is used. Ties are broken by computerised random allocation. Appendix 1 gives each community school's OS measuring point and 'distance priority radius' (1FE 500m, 2FE 750m, 3FE 1000m, 4FE 1250m). Community oversubscription criteria: 5 sibling within radius, 7 nearest within radius, 8 sibling outside radius, 9 nearest outside radius. Frithwood reserves 5 places for a nodal point. Harmondsworth and Heathrow use defined boundary areas instead of a radius. The Sept 2027 primary leaflet repeats that distance is measured in a straight line from the OS point at the home to a fixed point in the school. Every own-admission-authority summary in the Sept 2027 brochure that states a method also uses a straight line (e.g. Hillside to grid ref 510150 191063, Oak Farm to E507730 N183934, Laurel Lane main entrance to main entrance, Wood End Park to the main gate, Brookside/Hewens/Rosedale to the reception point). William Byrd gives priority to a defined area.

Hounslow.method_notes: Starting School in Hounslow (Sept 2027 brochure, 'Distance' definition, p.34): for community schools and any own-admission-authority school whose policy uses the LA measuring system, distance is the WALKING route measured by GIS (Synergy/School Admissions Management, Access UK) along OS MasterMap Highways Network road centrelines, from the LLPG/NLPG 'seed point' in the home address footprint, via the nearest network node, to the nearest school gate used by pupils. Equal distances are randomly ordered by the LA database. Community school oversubscription order: looked after, exceptional medical/social need, siblings, children of staff, distance. Academies, free schools and VA faith schools set their own criteria (faith, priority admission areas, Pupil Premium, nearest-school); the brochure refers them to the common definition, so walking is assumed unless stated. Figures are in miles.

Islington.method_notes: Islington Community School Determined Admission Arrangements 2026-27 (Admission Criteria to Islington Community Primary Schools, criterion 4 Distance): nearness is determined by a computerised mapping system using a straight-line distance measurement from the home address (as defined by the Land & Property Gazetteer) to the midpoint of the school grounds (as determined by Islington LA). Kensington & Chelsea.method_notes: RBKC admission arrangements for community primary schools 2026-27, criterion 5: 'Children living nearest to the school calculated as a straight line... to the main entrance of the school building used by pupils. For any school that has more than one entrance... the entrance of the main school reception will be used as the measuring point', using the Council's computerised measuring system. Accessibility by car or public transport is disregarded. Applicants sharing an address point, or at exactly the same distance, are separated by random allocation. Fox Primary: places inside a designated priority area are allocated by random allocation, then by straight-line distance for applicants outside it. Exceptions from the brochure summaries: Christ Church CofE uses the shortest walking route; Holy Trinity CofE measures to a midpoint between its Cadogan Gardens and Sedding Street sites; Ark Brunel measures to the centre of the school grounds; Kensington Primary Academy to its main gate on Kensington High Street; St Francis of Assisi and St Mary's Catholic from the front door of the home. Kingston.method_notes: Kingston (admissions run by Achieving for Children) uses a straight-line measurement in metres from a grid reference point within the home property supplied by Ordnance Survey (the 'seed point') to the closest named school gate set out in the school's admission arrangements, calculated by the council's GIS; only GIS distances are used. Lambeth.method_notes: Lambeth community schools (LA as admission authority): distance is a straight line measured by a computerised mapping system from a point at the home address identified via the Local Land and Property Gazetteer (LLPG) to a central point in the school's grounds as profiled in the software. Closest-first tie-breaker; equal distances resolved by random allocation (Synergy). Exceptions: Henry Cavendish (two sites) uses nodal points (Balham: Hydethorpe Road; Streatham: Dingley Lane); Sudbourne has a different proximity point (measured from the Mandrell Road site per brochure); Kingswood measured to the upper site. Own-admission-authority schools vary: Christ Church Streatham (pedestrian gate), St Leonard's (pupil gate), St Luke's (Linton Grove entrance), Corpus Christi (main reception entrance), Dunraven (North Site entrance), Rosendale (central point as council). Walking routes are used by Iqra (walking distance), Orchard (safest walking route) and Julian's (shortest walking route). All 'last distance' columns in the community allocation tables are headed 'Last distance - straight line (metres)'. Sources: Determined 2026-27 Lambeth school admissions arrangements (criterion 5, p.7-8) and the 2026-27 primary admissions brochure.

Lewisham.method_notes: Lewisham community primary admission arrangements (criterion 5 'Distance to school', as printed in 'Applying to start primary school in September 2027' booklet p11-12 and the council's community admissions policy page): distance measured in a straight line using the Local Authority's computerised distance measuring system, from the address point of the child's permanent home (NLPG eastings/northings, usually within the property footprint) to a designated point within the school. Booklet p23 says 2026 distances were measured electronically in metres to a 'central point within the school premises' / 'a point in the school premises as determined by the Ordnance Survey'; the 2024 grid says 'a nodal point within the school premises'. Criteria order: looked-after children, exceptional medical/social need, siblings, children of staff, distance. Ties: same block of flats -> lowest door number; otherwise drawing lots (witnessed). Twins etc. admitted as excepted pupils. Stillness Infant: sibling criterion includes Stillness Junior. The council grid covers community schools only; academies, free schools and VA faith schools are their own admission authorities.

Merton.method_notes: Merton community schools: distance measured in a straight line by Merton Admissions' computerised Geographical Information System, from a start point plotted within the applicant's home property to the main school reception entrance; ties broken by random allocation. Dundonald, Wimbledon Chase and Wimbledon Park give priority to children inside an Admissions Priority Area before distance. Academies, free school and VA faith schools are their own admission authorities with their own criteria (Source: Merton community school admission arrangements 2026-27, s.4.5.5; Reception 2025 booklet).

Newham.method_notes: Newham LA Determined Admission Arrangements (Sept 2027 entry, printed in the 'Starting school in September 2027' booklet pp59-80), adopted by all Newham community, VC, academy and free schools except Harris Academy Chobham and the Catholic/CofE VA faith schools. Tie-break within each criterion is shortest home-to-school walking distance, calculated by an industry GIS in miles to 3 decimal places. Start: the address point in the Council's Local Land and Property Gazetteer (LLPG; blocks of flats use the block's point), joined by a 'dogleg' to the nearest point of the OS MasterMap Highways Network. End: the school's nominated entrance, i.e. the main gate at the official postal address unless the governing body notifies another (p79: Central Park Primary - Loxford Avenue E6; St Joachim's RC Primary - Front Main Entrance of Newham Dockside). Route uses adopted highways and approved footpaths; excludes parks (the Greenway is included), unofficial crossings of A-roads and the DLR, Royal Docks crossings other than official bridges, and commercial/residential car parks. Out-of-borough applicants: straight line from the nearest highway point to the borough boundary, then walking. Equal distances: lower floor in flats first, otherwise random draw. Booklet notes some academies that do not adopt these arrangements use straight-line distance or random allocation; Harris Academy Chobham's offer table gives its tie-break as straight-line distance. The Catholic schools and St Luke's CofE use shortest walking distance.

Shaftesbury 2026, Stratford Manor 2026/2025, Earlham 2024, St Antony's 2024, St Joachim's 2025 and St Francis' 2026 were full (or over) but still show N/A, with the last places going to LA alternative allocations, so they are also treated as all_offered: an inference. Ellen Wilkinson 2024 (56 of 60) and Kensington 2024 (69 of 90) print a distance although the totals show spare places; the distances are kept as printed. St Helen's 2024 and St Winefride's 2024 last offers were under faith criterion 'FPG9' (as printed). The St Luke's 2025 total was not transcribed. Excluded: Calverton Primary (closed 31 Aug 2026) and Odessa Infant (closed 31 Aug 2026 when it merged into St James' CofE), plus junior schools Godwin and Lathom. St James' CofE Primary (VC, E7 9DA) became an all-through primary from Sept 2026 by absorbing Odessa Infant, so it has no reception offer history under its own name; it is recorded as not_published. Odessa's own tables showed all applicants offered in 2026 (44 of 60), 2025 (26 of 60) and 2024 (47 of 90). PAN is the 'Actual Places' for Sept 2026 (published admission numbers can be higher). Redbridge.method_notes: LB Redbridge Admission Arrangements for Community Primary and Secondary Schools 2027-28 (paras 1.9, 3.3 and Note 3) use shortest (safe) walking distance, measured by a Geographic Information System from the child's home to the main entrance of the school along public roads and recognised footpaths. For flats in the same block the distance is measured from the block's main entrance. Recognised routes must be paved or tarmac, lit, well maintained and accessible at all times, so informal paths and paths across private land may be excluded; routes are fixed before the admissions round. Equal distances are settled by random allocation in the Synergy admissions system. Sibling priority lapses if the family has moved more than one mile from the school since the sibling's offer (offer-day sheets). Community primaries have no catchment areas, so the order is LAC, staff children, siblings, then distance. Seven Kings (all-through community school) and Loxford (all-through academy) give catchment priority. Faith and own-admission-authority schools (Al-Noor, Atam, Avanti Court, OLOL, Wanstead Church, the Catholic and Jewish schools) use faith banding or criteria; the council sheet reports their last band.

Some kept 2025 and 2026 distances are large (Oakdale Infants 9.408 and 5.044, Gilbert Colvin 5.290, Manford 3.694 miles) and may mean the school was barely oversubscribed; they are recorded as printed. For faith and banded schools (Al-Noor, Atam, Avanti Court, OLOL, Wanstead Church, Seven Kings, Loxford) the value recorded is the last band or criterion listed, with the other bands in criterion_note; Avanti Court 2026 offered no places to Band 4 (non-faith). Richmond.method_notes: Council (Achieving for Children) measures home-to-school distance in metres as the shortest route by road and/or maintained footpath using the School Admissions GIS and Ordnance Survey data. Start: OS address/seed point within the property (route joins nearest road centre; all flats in a block share one point). End: nearest named (pedestrian) school gate or nodal point designated in the school's admission arrangements. Excludes routes through car parks, parks, cemeteries, private paths etc.; council says these are not promoted as actual walking routes. Exceptions per council guide (2026 and 2027 entry): Deer Park, St Elizabeth's Catholic Primary, Thomson House and Twickenham Primary Academy measure in a straight line from the seed point to school-designated gate(s). Faith schools (VA/Catholic academies) allocate many places by faith/parish criteria first. Sources: Richmond primary guide 2027 entry (Sep 2026) and 2026 entry; Admission arrangements for Richmond community schools 2027/28.

Southwark.method_notes: Southwark community school admission arrangements 2026/27 (also printed in 'Starting primary school in Southwark 2027/28' pp20-21), criterion 5: children living nearest to the school as measured by a straight line from the child's home to the main school gate/entrance. Note (e): the LA uses the eastings and northings linked to the applicant's address, generated by its Capita pupil database; blocks of flats with a communal entrance use the grid reference of the block, with lower door numbers taking priority. Ivydale (two sites) is measured to the main gate/entrance of both sites and the shorter distance used. Tie-break: straight-line distance, then drawing lots; multiple births admitted as excepted pupils. Criteria: LAC/previously LAC, EHCP-named, medical/social need, siblings, children of permanent staff (capped per form of entry), distance. Own-admission-authority schools mostly also use straight line (to main entrance, main gate, school entrance or site centre); St Peter's CofE and St Joseph's Gomm Road use walking distance; Angel Oak's summary gives no distance criterion.

Tower Hamlets.method_notes: Tower Hamlets oversubscription criteria for community schools (Starting Primary School in Tower Hamlets 2027 prospectus, 'Oversubscription criteria and tie-break', p16): EHCP first; then 1 looked-after/previously looked-after, 2 medical/social, 3 in-catchment siblings, 4 children of staff, 5 in-catchment children for whom it is their nearest community school in the catchment, 6 other in-catchment, 7 out-of-catchment siblings, 8 others. Tie-break within criteria 3-8: shortest walking distance, measured with a digital Ordnance Survey map from the centre point of the address to the centre point of the school's designated main entrance along the centre line of the shortest approved route (local footpaths and public walkways, with regard to safety; ignores crossing points); equal distances by random allocation. Six catchment areas (Stepney, Bow, Poplar, Isle of Dogs, Wapping, Bethnal Green). The council's 'tie-break cut off distance' is the walking distance of the last child offered, within whichever criterion places ran out, so it is not a simple radius: in-catchment applicants beat closer out-of-catchment ones. Academies that delegate admissions to the LA and use these criteria: Culloden, Old Ford, Solebay (Paradigm), Bygrove, Mulberry Canon Barnett, Mulberry Wood Wharf, Stebon, St Paul's Way Trust, The Clara Grant (prospectus p15). VA/faith schools, Canary Wharf College and Sir William Burrough have their own arrangements.

Waltham Forest.method_notes: Waltham Forest community and VC school criteria (Starting Primary School 2027 brochure, Section 1, pp11-13): distance is measured in a straight line from the centre of the child's permanent address, as defined by the Local Land and Property Gazetteer, to the designated main gate of the school. Measurement uses the RouteFinder GIS system, in miles. In multi-occupancy buildings the lowest door number takes priority; remaining ties go to a lottery drawn by an impartial officer. Barclay, Mission Grove and Hillyfield are split-site schools: both sites are measured and the shorter distance used. Several academies adopt the LA criteria (Barclay, Davies Lane, George Mitchell, Hillyfield, Mayville, Riverley, Roger Ascham, Selwyn, Sybourn, Thomas Gamuel, Willow Brook, Woodford Green, Yardley). Exceptions: Lime Academy Larkswood measures the walking route on AA route planner to the main gate. Buxton School measures straight line to its Woodhouse Road main gate. The United Learning Trust schools (Salisbury Manor, Longshaw, Whittingham, Walthamstow Primary Academy), Woodside (REAch2), Emmanuel (free school) and the Catholic/CofE schools have their own criteria. Where the brochure states their method it is straight line to the main gate.

The 2025 figures come only from the 2025/26 column of the 3-year table: the Starting Primary School 2026 brochure, which holds the detailed 2025 table, was not found online. Blank cells mean 'all on-time applicants were offered this school or a higher preference' and are recorded as all_offered. Dawlish 2026 and St Joseph's Infant 2026 were full but show no cut-off, so they are also all_offered. Oakhill 2024 printed 5.772 miles (kept as printed). St Mary's CofE 2026 (0.305) was a multiple-birth case. PAN is the 2026 PAN from the offer-day table. The criteria of the ULT schools, Woodside, Emmanuel and the faith schools were not read in full, so their method is assumed straight line where not stated. Junior schools (Chapel End Junior Academy, St Joseph's Catholic Junior) are excluded.

Wandsworth.method_notes: Straight-line distance from the location of the home property to the central point of the school site, as determined by Wandsworth Council's Geographical Information System; measurements by other systems/to other points not accepted; ties broken at random (Wandsworth community school admissions policies, Note 4/5). The 'Choose a Wandsworth Primary School' brochure (Sept 2027 entry) says distance is measured in a straight line between home and the centre of the school site, with all measurements calculated by the council GIS. Exceptions: Belleville Primary distances measured to its main Webb's Road site; priority areas used by Beatrix Potter, Furzedown, Penwortham, Sellincourt, Franciscan and St Michael's CE; faith schools apply faith/parish criteria before distance. All figures are 'furthest distance offered' on national offer day (16 April), in metres.

Wandsworth.gaps: PAN is null for schools where every applicant was offered (the docs give no figures for those rows). Postcodes for open schools come from the council brochure; GIAS was not checked. Honeywell Junior School omitted (not a Reception entry point). Broadwater Primary closed Aug 2024 and does not appear in any of the three docs. Some PDF tables were garbled when extracted: Belleville Wix class/column mapping, St Faith's and St Mary's Putney column mapping, and Gatton 2024 criterion are lower-confidence; Penwortham 2024 printed as '491mm'. Faith schools in some years publish only category counts with no distance (status not_published). Academy/free school/VA policies were not individually checked for measurement method; the council brochure says all distances are calculated by the council GIS, so straight_line is assumed for all. The 2026 'apply for a primary school place 2026' PDF could not be fetched.

Westminster.method_notes: Westminster community schools (summarised criteria in the 'Your choice for primary education 2027' brochure, matching the determined admission arrangements 2027/28): final criterion 'Children living nearest to the school calculated as a straight line measurement from the child's home "address point" determined by Ordnance Survey data to the main entrance of the school building used by pupils', using the Council's geographical measuring system. Brochure figures are 'of a mile'/'miles' and are the distance reached for the last offer on that criterion. Exceptions found: Millbank Gardens, Pimlico Primary (Future Academies), St Peter's Chippenham Mews and St Matthew's use shortest walking route; St Augustine's tie-break is by walking route; Soho Parish measures to the centre of the school grounds; Gateway Academy to its nearest pupil entrance; Ark King Solomon to the midpoint between its two sites' entrances; St John's Wood Primary to the Bridgeman Street main entrance; St Saviour's to its Shirland Road entrance. Many VA schools fill most places on faith criteria first.

Units are as printed: 'of a mile' is recorded as miles. Brochure pages were parsed by text extraction, and the 2024 two-up spreads were checked against rendered images. The measuring method of VA schools whose summaries don't state one is assumed to be the council's straight-line default. PANs come from the 2027 brochure (Edward Wilson's was 56 in earlier years).
